headline: OpenAI's Jalapeño AI ASIC unveiled at Hot Chips 2026
summary: The company's custom AI accelerator, developed with AI assistance, promises efficiency and throughput gains over existing hardware.
details: OpenAI has revealed details about its custom AI accelerator, codenamed "Jalapeño," at the Hot Chips 2026 conference. This specialized chip is designed to enhance AI model performance, focusing on efficiency and throughput.

Notably, the Jalapeño ASIC was developed with the assistance of AI itself, a meta-approach that OpenAI claims contributed to its advanced design. The chip aims to outperform current industry standards, including Nvidia's Blackwell architecture.

While specific performance benchmarks were not fully detailed, the "Jalapeño Intelligence Processor" is presented as a significant step towards more powerful and efficient AI hardware. The development highlights OpenAI's increasing investment in custom silicon.

The presentation at Hot Chips 2026 provided a glimpse into the future of AI hardware development, showcasing how AI can be leveraged not only to run models but also to design the very chips that power them.

headline_marked: Plaud One Earphones [[Record Calls & Control AI Remotely]] with eSIM
headline: Plaud One Earphones Record Calls & Control AI Remotely with eSIM
summary: These new AI-powered earbuds can record conversations and use an eSIM-enabled case to let users instruct AI agents without a phone or computer.
details: Plaud is launching its new AI-powered earphones, Plaud One, designed for recording calls and in-person conversations. The earbuds feature active noise cancellation and 12mm drivers, offering six hours of recording time on a single charge. The accompanying case, which supports an eSIM, can capture voices within a five-meter range and extends the total recording time to 25 hours.

What sets the Plaud One apart is its AI agent integration. After transcribing conversations, the AI can connect to tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, and Slack to perform tasks such as writing follow-up emails or creating documents. The case's eSIM functionality allows users to issue commands to these AI agents remotely, without needing their phone or computer.

While software solutions for call transcription and AI task automation exist, Plaud One aims to offer a more integrated hardware-software experience. The company is also developing further agentic capabilities expected in future updates, and early buyers will receive $200 in credits for AI tasks.

Plaud One is available for pre-order at $249 and is slated to ship in the fourth quarter of 2026. Buyers receive 300 minutes of free transcription monthly, with additional plans starting at $8.33 per month (paid annually). This limited release is intended to gauge market demand for AI-focused earphones.

The company, which claims an annual run-rate revenue of $100 million, faces stiff competition from other hardware note-takers and software solutions. Plaud's CEO, Nathan Xu, emphasizes the need for a wearable, always-ready interface for AI, positioning the earbuds as a socially acceptable and private solution.
